title: The elder
hookLine: Orthodox Christians seek a spiritual father or mother for guidance

lines: SPEAK, LORD; FOR THY SERVANT HEARETH.
cards: Night, in the temple of the Lord. A boy named Samuel, who serves there, hears his name called and runs to the old priest Eli. Here I am, he says.
Eli says, I didn't call you. Go back and lie down. It happens again, and again.

Eli is old, his eyes growing dim, but he's the one who works out what's going on: the Lord is calling the boy. So he tells Samuel what to say if it comes once more: "Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth."
Eli doesn't hear the voice himself. He helps someone else hear it. That's the picture behind today's word, from the Russian Orthodox tradition: starets.

teach.b: Starets, in Russian, simply means an old man, but the role isn't really about age.

An elder is a monk, sometimes a nun, now and then a lay person, known for prayer and for seeing clearly into hearts, whom others seek out for guidance. A woman in the role is a staritsa; in Greek the elder is a geron.
Tradition traces the role back to the desert, where people walked out to an old monk's cell and said, in substance, Abba, give me a word. Not a lecture: one sentence to live on for a while.
Abba means father; a woman teacher was called amma, mother. Why need this? Because watchfulness, tears and the prayer rope can all be bent by the one doing them.
A mind can mistake its own pride for holiness, and never notice. Proverbs puts it plainly: "Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety."
The elder is a second pair of eyes on the soul.
Dostoevsky put an elder at the heart of The Brothers Karamazov, Father Zosima, and described the bond as freely handing your will to someone wiser, for the sake of becoming free.
That's the strong form: a long, trusted relationship, not advice on demand. In everyday Orthodox life, this guidance can come through a priest who hears confession and becomes a spiritual father.
Other churches use other names: Catholics speak of spiritual direction, and some Protestants of a mentor or a pastor.

how: Orthodox Christians seek guidance from a spiritual father or mother, who may be the priest who hears their confession; some travel to monasteries to ask a recognized elder for a word.

o: a wise guide others seek out for counsel in prayer
a bishop's title in the Russian church
the oldest monk, who rules over a monastery

p: Russian for an old man, an elder
helped the boy hear the voice

s: a starets has to be very old
the word means an old man, but the role is about prayer and clear sight, not age.
in the desert, people asked a monk for a single word to live on
abba, give me a word: one sentence, not a lecture.
in the story, old Eli hears God's voice himself
Eli doesn't hear it. he helps the boy hear it: speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth.

games.q: you're old Eli. the boy has woken you again, sure you called him. what do you tell him?
o: go back to sleep, you're dreaming.
if it comes again, say: speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth.
tell me what the voice says, and I'll decide what it means.
games.why: Eli sends Samuel back with a line to say. the old priest doesn't take over; he helps the boy listen for himself.

practice: Let one question rise, something you've been deciding on your own, and then let a face come to mind: someone you trust who sees more clearly than you on this, a grandparent, a pastor, an old friend, a teacher.
Imagine asking them, and wonder what they might see that you can't. If you pray, you can say Samuel's line: Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth.

wordCard.voice: Starets. The elder: someone seasoned in prayer whom others seek out for guidance, a second pair of eyes on the soul.

orig.note: Russian: an old man, an elder. In Greek the word is γέρων, geron.

carryVoice: Your line: go to the elder. Nobody has to see their own soul alone. Until tomorrow.
